correctness.rationale: The classification step is proved from first principles: a closed convex set containing a hyperplane is invariant under that hyperplane's direction and hence is the inverse image of a closed interval; properness makes the direction unique. Face structure then reduces to interval intersections within one normal class. The explicit minimal-right-endpoint elimination gives a valid 1-collapse, with a separate argument for right-unbounded intervals and for universal vertices.

value.rationale: The result resolves the codimension-one boundary case of a newly explicit open problem. The case is structurally distinguished because quotienting by the unique hyperplane direction reduces the geometry to intervals, yielding an explicit collapse order. The primary source identifies collapsibility as a route to stronger fractional and selection-structure consequences, so the boundary theorem has a concrete role beyond classification.
